context_items.value: Namoi and Gwydir regions, northwest New South Wales
context_items.quote: We chose to focus on the Namoi and Gwydir regions in northwest NSW, as production in this area is strongly representative of Australian cotton production (Hedayati, 2015).

also_stated.quote: The geographical scope of the LCA was the cotton growing region of northwest NSW Australia, in the Namoi-Gwydir regions including the towns of Narrabri, Moree and Walgett.

context_items.value: three production seasons, 2011-2012 to 2013-2014
context_items.quote: The temporal scope of the LCA was the three cotton production seasons of 2011-2012, 2012-2013, and 2013-2014.

context_items.value: one tonne of cotton lint from continuous cotton, delivered for export at port
context_items.quote: The functional unit of the LCA study was one metric tonne cotton fibre (lint) produced in a continuous cotton production system and delivered for export at port.

also_stated.quote: with a functional unit of one tonne of cotton lint at port

context_items.value: life cycle assessment of climate change impact only
context_items.quote: The scope of the environmental assessment was limited to climate change impact.

also_stated.quote: Whilst LCA can be applied across a broad array of impact categories, we limited this study to the climate change impact of cotton production on GHG emissions.
We applied the LCA method to calculate the GHG emissions profile of cotton production and associated GHG mitigation strategies.

context_items.value: system boundary: pre-farm, on-farm and post-farm stages (cradle to port)
context_items.quote: The system boundary of the LCA study (Fig. 1) included the pre-farm stage (i.e. production and transport of raw materials), the on-farm stage (i.e. cotton farming practices) and the post-farm stage (i.e. cotton ginning and the transport of cotton lint to an export port).

context_items.value: emissions formulae and factors from the Australian National Inventory Report
context_items.quote: we applied emissions formulae and factors from the Australian National Inventory Report, except where more specific published data were available.

context_items.value: economic allocation of emissions between lint and cottonseed
context_items.quote: we considered economic allocation as the most appropriate means of partitioning, despite the dynamic nature of commodity prices.

also_stated.quote: We applied an average cotton lint price from 2011 to 2014 of $2070/t ($470/bale) and average cottonseed price of $300/t, allocating approximately 86% of the life cycle climate change impact to lint.

context_items.value: biogenic CO2 (absorbed by the crop, released from residues) excluded
context_items.quote: we excluded CO2 absorbed by the cotton crop during its growth and the CO2 released from the decomposition of cotton residues in the field (i.e. biogenic CO2) from the primary LCA.

also_stated.quote: Whilst biogenic carbon was excluded from the primary LCA on the basis of consistency with the IPCC (IPCC, 2006) and NIR, we also questioned the sensitivity of the emissions profile to this assumption.

context_items.value: process flows under 1% of mass or energy excluded
context_items.quote: All process flows with a cumulative mass or energy of less than 1% were excluded, e.g. packaging glues used at the cotton gin.

context_items.value: soil carbon sequestration not included
context_items.quote: Opportunities to sequester carbon may also be available but were not included in the primary assessment of this paper due to uncertainties.

context_items.value: soil organic N at a steady state
context_items.quote: We also assumed that background levels of soil organic N had reached a steady state.
